interpretation: Instruction: 'Pick up the green tape and place it on the black shelf'. The green tape is obj1 at the start: a green tape ring lying flat on the table, centre (0.250, 0.0135), inner radius ~0.0325 m, outer radius ~0.0446 m (8.9 cm across, wider than the gripper's 0.066 m max_width), height ~0.025 m (wall ~1.2 cm thick). The black shelf is obj2: a solid black box 26 x 14 x 8 cm, long axis along y, flat top at z=0.080 spanning x 0.36-0.50, y -0.144-0.116. Goal state: the tape ring lifted off the table and resting on top of the black box, fully on its top face, released by the gripper. Nothing ambiguous beyond 'shelf' meaning the black box; it is a solid box (no opening), so 'on' means its top face.
plan: Initial plan: top-down pinch of the ring's wall (the ring is too wide to grasp across), closing axis radial, lift, carry over the shelf, lower until the ring is a few mm above the top, open, retract. IK scans showed that on this PiPER the top-down orientation is height-limited (max top-down TCP z ~0.09 at x=0.40, ~0.05 at x=0.45, none at x=0.50), while holding the ring above the 8 cm shelf needs TCP z ~0.11 at x ~0.43, so top-down placement was infeasible. Revised plan: use rh.side_pose(azimuth 0, tilt 65 deg), i.e. the approach tilted 25 deg forward from vertical, with the closing axis horizontal along y, and grip the ring's -y wall. There the wall is normal to y, so the pads stay parallel to it even with the forward tilt, and because the grasp and the placement use the same orientation the ring stays level throughout. With this pose every height from z 0.02 to 0.21 is reachable at both the grasp and place positions. I picked the -y side over +y because its joint-limit margins were at least 0.2 rad at every key pose (the +y side had 0.07-0.09 at placement). After the lift I measured the ring's offset from the TCP with the cloud and set the place pose so that the ring centre would land at the shelf-top centre (0.43, -0.014).

steps.what: Read the embodiment and the scene (observe, objects, all three cameras, 3D views, close-ups).
steps.why: Identify the robot, gripper limits and the objects named in the instruction.
steps.result: agilex_piper_sim, 6 joints, parallel jaw (stroke 0.07, max_width 0.066, closed_empty 0.97, held_below 0.93, tip_reach 0.02), cameras left/right/wrist; budget 2250 steps at dt=1/15 s. obj1 = green tape ring, obj2 = black box shelf (top z 0.080).

steps.what: Measured the ring (circle fit on its points) and the shelf top (heightmap, OBB).
steps.why: Ring too wide to grasp across, so the wall position and thickness are needed for a wall pinch; also needed the shelf top height and extent.

steps.what: IK scans of top-down poses (8 grasp sides x 2 yaws, heights 0.02-0.25).
steps.why: Check that the pick, lift and place poses are reachable before moving.
steps.result: Top-down poses unreachable above z ~0.14 near the ring and above ~0.09 at x 0.40 (none at x 0.50), so a top-down place on the shelf was infeasible. Switched to a 25 deg forward-tilted side_pose (tilt 65), which reaches z 0.02-0.21 at every needed xy; chose to grip the -y wall (joint margins >= 0.2 rad).

steps.what: Moved to pre-grasp, TCP (0.247, -0.025, 0.09), tilted pose, gripper open (49 steps).
steps.why: Get above the -y wall of the ring at the grasp orientation.
steps.result: Reached (0.242, -0.024, 0.089), step 49. A wrist-camera cloud re-fit confirmed the ring centre (0.2499, 0.0134) and the -y wall middle at y -0.0249 (target -0.0251).

steps.what: Descended straight down to TCP z 0.028 (34 steps).
steps.why: Straddle the wall with the fingertips ~1 cm above the table.
steps.result: Reached (0.243, -0.022, 0.027), step 83. The wrist and scene cameras show the inner finger in the ring's hole and the outer finger outside it.
gripper_measured 0.861, gap 9.7 mm (< held_below 0.93): the wall is held. Step 98.

steps.what: Lifted straight up to TCP z 0.15 (49 steps).
steps.why: Raise the ring above the shelf height (ring bottom must clear z 0.080).
steps.result: The ring came off the table with the gripper, step 147. Colour-filtered cloud: ring level, bottom ~0.029 below the TCP, centre offset (+0.003, +0.036) from the TCP; a side render shows it held horizontal.

steps.what: Transferred horizontally at z 0.15 to TCP (0.427, -0.050) (56 steps).
steps.why: Put the ring centre over the shelf-top centre (0.43, -0.014), with the ring bottom ~4 cm above the shelf.
steps.result: Reached (0.431, -0.051, 0.150), step 203; measured ring centre (0.433, -0.016), footprint x 0.388-0.478 and y -0.060-0.029, inside the shelf top.

steps.why: Bring the ring bottom to within a few mm of the shelf top before releasing.
steps.result: Reached z 0.110, step 245; the ring is on or just above the shelf top, still held (0.855). check_batch flagged finger-sphere contacts with the shelf (to -1.1 cm). I judged these to be the sphere model reaching past the fingers, since the real fingertips (tip_reach 0.02, ~1.8 cm below the TCP at this tilt) stay ~1.2 cm above the shelf top. The images showed no finger contact.

steps.why: Release the ring onto the shelf.
steps.result: gripper_measured 0.0; the ring rests flat on the shelf top, step 260.

steps.what: Retracted straight up to TCP z 0.19 (42 steps).
steps.why: Lift the fingers clear of the ring (the inner finger was inside the hole) without disturbing it.
steps.result: Step 302; the ring stayed in place, seen in the left, right and wrist cameras.

steps.what: Final verification (reperceive, cloud, annotate on both scene cameras), then finish_episode.
steps.why: Check each part of the instruction from fresh images before ending.
steps.result: Ring top at z 0.1051 (= 0.080 + 0.025, lying flat), centre (0.4275, -0.0151), footprint x 0.383-0.472 and y -0.060-0.029, inside the shelf top. Perception merged the ring and shelf into obj3, and obj4 is the shelf top seen through the ring's hole; both are expected artefacts of touching objects. finish_episode at step 302 of 2250.

key_images.caption: Start, left camera with ids: obj1 green tape ring on the table, obj2 black box shelf.
Close-up of the tape ring (~9 cm across, 2.5 cm tall, ~1.2 cm wall): too wide for the 6.6 cm gripper, so the wall is pinched.
Wrist camera at grasp height: the open fingers straddle the ring's -y wall (inner finger in the hole).
Wrist camera after closing: fingers pinch the wall, gripper_measured 0.861 (held).
Left camera after lifting to TCP z 0.15: the ring is off the table in the gripper.
3D render from the side: the ring hangs level, its bottom above the shelf-top height.
Left camera: the ring lowered onto the shelf top, still held.
Final, left camera: the tape ring lies flat on top of the black shelf, gripper open and retracted.
Final, right camera: the ring is on the shelf top, inside its edges.
Final, wrist camera from above: the ring lies flat on the shelf top, well inside its edges.

lessons: 1) On this PiPER sim the top-down orientation is height-limited (wrist joint5 limit +-1.22 rad): scan reachable heights with ik_batch before planning a place onto a raised surface. A 20-25 deg forward tilt (side_pose azimuth 0, tilt 65-70) reached z 0.02-0.21 across x 0.25-0.43. 2) For a ring wider than the gripper, pinch its wall with the closing axis radial. Grip it at the ring's +-y side so the forward tilt (a rotation about y) keeps the closing axis horizontal and normal to the wall, and keep the same orientation from grasp to place so the ring stays level. 3) The reached TCP differed from the command by up to ~4-7 mm, so leave at least 2 cm of placement margin and re-measure the held object's offset from the TCP after lifting. 4) Finger collision spheres report contacts ~1 cm past the real fingertips; judge real clearance with tip_reach_m and the images. 5) After placing, perception merges the object with its support (and splits off the support patch seen through a hole), so verify with colour-filtered cloud points and circle fits rather than object ids.
